solutions.latex:
The curve $y=x^2-3x$ is below the $x$-axis for $1\le x<3$ and above it for $3<x\le5$, so the two regions must be done separately.

$$\text{Area}=\left|\int_1^3(x^2-3x)\,dx\right|+\int_3^5(x^2-3x)\,dx$$

$$=\left|\left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}-\dfrac{3x^2}{2}\right]_1^3\right|+\left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}-\dfrac{3x^2}{2}\right]_3^5$$

$$=\left|\left(9-\dfrac{27}{2}\right)-\left(\dfrac13-\dfrac32\right)\right|+\left(\dfrac{125}{3}-\dfrac{75}{2}-\left(9-\dfrac{27}{2}\right)\right)=\left|-\dfrac{10}{3}\right|+\dfrac{26}{3}=\dfrac{36}{3}=12\text{ units}^2$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: separating the regions; 1: correct integration; 1: correct arithmetic

$$=\left|6-10\ln5-(0-10\ln2)\right|+10-10\ln7-(6-10\ln5)$$

$$=-6+10\ln5-10\ln2+4-10\ln7+10\ln5=20\ln5-10\ln2-10\ln7-2=10\ln\left(\dfrac{25}{14}\right)-2$$ (by the log laws)

$$AB=\dfrac{8}{\sin\theta}+\dfrac{1}{\cos\theta}$$

$AB=8(\sin\theta)^{-1}+(\cos\theta)^{-1}$

$$\dfrac{dAB}{d\theta}=-8(\sin\theta)^{-2}\cos\theta-(\cos\theta)^{-2}\cdot(-\sin\theta)=\dfrac{-8\cos\theta}{\sin^2\theta}+\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos^2\theta}=\dfrac{-8\cos^3\theta+\sin^3\theta}{\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta}$$

(Many students couldn't do the differentiation correctly.)

Set $\dfrac{dAB}{d\theta}=0$: $-8\cos^3\theta+\sin^3\theta=0$, so $\sin^3\theta=8\cos^3\theta$, $\tan^3\theta=8$, $\tan\theta=2$, $\theta\doteq63^\circ$.

$$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\theta & 60^\circ & 63^\circ & 65^\circ\\ \hline \frac{dAB}{d\theta} & -1.6 & 0 & 0.93\end{array}$$

The gradient goes from negative to positive, so this is a minimum.

$AB=\dfrac{8}{\sin63^\circ}+\dfrac{1}{\cos63^\circ}=11.18$ m
